column1: # Undo classification (#1813): every command in PdfCommandRegistry, and what happens to the undo history when it runs.
# Enforced by Excise.App.Tests/Unit/UndoClassificationTests.cs. A command missing from this file, a row for a command
# that no longer exists, or an unknown class fails the build. Adding a command therefore forces the question this file
# answers: does it change the open document, and if so, can it be undone?
#   Recorded      changes the open document (or pending edits) and pushes onto the undo stack. Evidence: a test file that
#                 calls UndoCommand. Annotation adds share one recorder (RecordAnnotationAdd / CommitRectAnnotationAsync),
#                 so their evidence is the shared mechanism, not one test per annotation kind.
#   ClearsHistory changes the open document IN PLACE and cannot be undone: clears the history, leaves the document
#                 reading as changed (#1812). Also Save/Open/Close, which are history boundaries. Evidence: a test that
#   WritesCopy    writes a new file; the open document is untouched, so there is nothing to undo.
#   OwnUndoSurface pending marks with their own per-item removal (redaction marks); not document edits.
#   CliOnly       automation with no GUI history.
#   NotMutating   navigation, view, search, tool arming, selection, printing, copying to the clipboard.
#   Gap           mutates and is not undoable yet. Evidence MUST name an open issue (#NNNN).
# What this file cannot see: mutations that have no registry command. Tool-arming commands (the draw, line,
# arrow, polygon, polyline and typewriter modes) are NotMutating here; the annotation or text box they create
# is committed by a pointer gesture and recorded by RecordAnnotationAdd / RecordTypewriterEdit, covered by
# UI/UndoRedoWorkflowTests.cs. A new gesture-only mutation needs its own test; this gate will not notice it.
